title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 29 (Public Offer of Securities to Be in Dematerialised Form)

content.overview: Section 29 requires every company making a public offer, and such other class or classes of public companies as may be prescribed, to issue the securities only in dematerialised form by complying with the provisions of the Depositories Act, 1996 and the regulations made thereunder. Prescribed unlisted companies may also be required to facilitate holding and transfer only in demat form.
content.glance: Public offers must be in demat form under the Depositories Act; prescribed classes of companies face the same rule; unlisted companies may be brought under demat-holding rules by prescription.
content.study: Section 29 is a form-of-issue rule. A company making a public offer of securities must issue them only in dematerialised form in accordance with the Depositories Act, 1996 and the regulations made under it. The Central Government may prescribe other classes of public companies that must also issue securities only in demat form. Further, such class or classes of unlisted companies as may be prescribed must facilitate dematerialisation of all their existing securities and issue and transfer securities only in demat form. Current-law framing: identify whether the issue is a public offer or falls within a prescribed class; then apply demat-only issue and the Depositories Act framework.

sections.body: Other prescribed classes of public companies must likewise issue only in demat form.

sections.heading: Prescribed Unlisted Companies
sections.body: Prescribed unlisted companies must facilitate dematerialisation of existing securities and issue and transfer only in demat form.
